**SEC. 129 – Constellation-class Frigate Program Limitation**
- **Limitation:** FY2025 Navy funds may not be obligated/expended for construction beyond the basic and functional design phase (as defined in 10 U.S.C. § 8669c) until the Secretary of Defense submits the required certification.
- **Certification:** Upon final approval of 95% of all basic and functional design drawings by the designated technical authority, the Secretary shall certify to the congressional defense committees that such drawings have been approved.
- **GAO Assessment:** Within 30 days of the Secretary’s certification, the Comptroller General shall submit to the committees an assessment of the Secretary’s compliance and the completeness of the design drawings.
- **Access:** The Secretary shall provide the Comptroller General timely access to necessary documents/information.

**SEC. 130 – Limitation on AH-1Z and UH-1Y Helicopter Upgrades**
- **Limitation:** The Secretary of the Navy may not carry out “covered upgrades” (structural improvements or electrical power upgrades) at a non-OEM facility until certifying to the Armed Services Committees that the plan is expected to: (1) match or exceed OEM-facility performance, survivability, lethality, interoperability, mission execution, and safety; (2) provide improved electrical power capacity and margin for future capabilities; (3) improve/expand future weapons interfaces; (4) allow improved ease of maintenance.

**SEC. 131 – Annual Report on Surface Ship Suppliers**
- **Requirement:** Not later than 180 days after enactment, and annually thereafter through September 30, 2029, the Secretary of the Navy shall submit a report analyzing surface ship component suppliers.
- **Elements:** (1) Assessment of each supplier’s status using the same/similar methodology as the Columbia-class submarine supplier evaluation tool; (2) if the supply base is at-risk, a stabilization action plan.

**SEC. 141 – Extension of RQ-4 Aircraft Limitations**
- Amends 10 U.S.C. § 9062(m)(1) by striking “September 30, 2028” and inserting “September 30, 2029” (extends minimum inventory requirement and related limitations).

**SEC. 142 – Annual Report on Air Force Tactical Fighter Aircraft Force Structure**
- Adds new 10 U.S.C. § 9062a.
- **Requirement:** Not later than April 1, 2025, and annually through 2029, the Secretary of the Air Force, in consultation with the Director of the Air National Guard and Commander of the Air Force Reserve Command, shall develop a 10-year tactical fighter aircraft force structure, recapitalization, training, and sustainment plan for active and reserve components, and submit a report.
- **Report Elements:** (1) Appropriate fighter mix and operational risk analyses; (2) procurement, divestment, and unit activation/deactivation/re-missioning plans fiscal year-by-fiscal year, unit-by-unit for 10 years; (3) actions to maintain operational readiness rates during recapitalization/modernization; (4) plans to augment/supplant piloted fighter capability with collaborative combat aircraft increment 1 or 2; (5) plans to augment/supplant training events with common, joint, all-domain, high-fidelity synthetic simulation environments.
- **Form:** Unclassified with graphs/tables/charts; may contain classified annex.
- **Definition:** “Fighter aircraft” has the meaning given in § 9062(i)(2).

**SEC. 143 – Modifications to Inventory Requirements for Certain Aircraft**
- (a) Amends § 133 of the FY2024 NDAA (P.L. 118-31): (1) Minimum primary mission aircraft inventory changed from “1,112 aircraft” to “1,101 aircraft”; (2) temporary exception date changed from “2024” to “2025”.
- (b) Amends § 134(d) of the FY2017 NDAA (P.L. 114-328): A-10 minimum inventory changed from “135 A-10 aircraft” to “96 A-10 aircraft”.

**SEC. 144 – Extension of Prohibition on E-3 AWACS Inventory Reductions**
- Amends § 142 of the FY2024 NDAA (P.L. 118-31) by inserting “or fiscal year 2025” after “fiscal year 2024”.

**SEC. 145 – Extension of C-130 Aircraft Requirements**
- (a) Amends § 146(a)(3)(B) of the FY2023 NDAA (P.L. 117-263), as amended, by striking “2024” and inserting “2025” (extends minimum inventory requirement).
- (b) Amends § 146(b)(1) of the same Act by striking “During fiscal years 2023 and 2024” and inserting “During the period of fiscal years 2023 through 2025” (extends prohibition on reduction of C-130s assigned to National Guard).

**SEC. 146 – Management of Temporary Relocation of B-1 Bomber Aircraft and Personnel**
- Amends § 133 of the FY2022 NDAA (P.L. 117-81), as amended, by redesignating subsection (c) as (d) and inserting new subsection (c).
- **New (c):** The Secretary of the Air Force shall, to the extent practicable, manage temporary relocation of B-1 aircraft/personnel resulting from planned military construction in a manner that: (1) minimizes effects to combat readiness; (2) mitigates risk of concentrating a significant number of the B-1 fleet at one location; (3) uses the construction period to maximize expeditionary actions (Bomber Task Force, Agile Combat Employment); (4) considers travel options/distance for families and dependents.

**SEC. 147 – Consolidation of Authorities Relating to Air Force Landing Gear**
- (a) The Secretary of the Air Force shall transfer to the Air Force Sustainment Center supply chain management, item management, and delegated engineering authorities for landing gear systems of F-15EX, F-22, F-35, and T-7A aircraft.
- (b) Within 120 days of enactment, the Secretary shall develop and initiate an implementation plan.
- (c) Within 30 days after completing the plan, the Secretary shall submit a report to the Armed Services Committees describing: (1) planned milestones; (2) data, staff, and funding needed; (3) progress in meeting milestones.

**SEC. 148 – Recapitalization of Air Refueling Tanker Aircraft of the Reserve Components**
- (a) The Secretary of the Air Force shall replace covered reserve KC-135 aircraft on a one-for-one basis with tanker aircraft having capabilities equivalent to or exceeding those being replaced.
- (b) Requirements: (1) May not reduce reserve component tanker inventory below FY2025 President’s budget levels; (2) if a reserve unit is assigned more KC-135s than are being replaced, remaining KC-135s shall stay within the reserve component for redistribution.
- (c) Waiver: The Secretary may waive the one-for-one replacement requirement on a case-by-case basis if replacement would degrade readiness.
- (d) Sunset: This section terminates on October 1, 2025.
- (e) Definition: “Covered reserve KC-135 aircraft” means a reserve component KC-135 identified for replacement with a KC-46 or later-generation tanker.

**SEC. 149 – Prohibition on Reduction of KC-135 Aircraft in PMAI of the Reserve Components**
- (a) FY2025 Air Force funds may not be obligated/expended to reduce the number of KC-135 aircraft designated as primary mission aircraft inventory (PMAI) within the reserve components.
- (b) PMAI defined per 10 U.S.C. § 9062(i)(2)(B).

**SEC. 150 – Prohibition on Retirement of F-15E Aircraft and Fighter Aircraft Capabilities Study**
- (a)(1) Prohibition: The Secretary of the Air Force may not retire, prepare to retire, or place in storage/backup status any F-15E aircraft until September 30, 2027.
- (a)(2) Exception: Does not apply to individual F-15E aircraft the Secretary determines, on a case-by-case basis, to be no longer mission capable and uneconomical to repair due to accidents, mishaps, or excessive material degradation/non-airworthiness.
- (a)(3) Supersedes inconsistent provisions of 10 U.S.C. § 9062(l).
- (b) Study: The Secretary of Defense shall seek to enter into a contract with a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC) to carry out: (A) an analysis of the Department of the Air Force fighter procurement, fielding, and divestment plan; (B) a fighter capability and requirements study estimating the number of fighter aircraft needed to meet combatant commander requirements.
- (b)(2) The FFRDC shall submit a report to the Secretary of Defense.
- (b)(3) Not later than March 15, 2026, the Secretary shall: (A) submit an unaltered copy of the FFRDC report to the congressional defense committees; (B) submit a separate report with the Secretary’s views, including a detailed explanation of strategy/methodology and assessed operational risk based on CJCS Manual 3105.01A; (C) provide a briefing.
- (c) “Fighter aircraft” defined as F-15, F-16, F-22, F-35, and Next Generation Air Dominance piloted combat aircraft.

**SEC. 151 – Notification of Delays in Delivery of MH-139 Aircraft**
- (a) Within 30 days of becoming aware of an expected delay in the delivery date of an MH-139 aircraft, the Secretary of the Air Force shall submit written notice and explanation to the Armed Services Committees.
- (b) “Delivery date” means the date expected under the most recent schedule in effect as of enactment.

**SEC. 152 – Plan and Requirements for Fielding Air Base Air Defense Sites**
- (a) The Secretary of the Air Force, in consultation with Commanders of USNORTHCOM, USEUCOM, and USINDOPACOM, shall develop and implement a plan to field air base air defense sites at Air Force installations and other priority sites.
- (b) Each site shall have capabilities: (1) expeditionary mobile protection; (2) fixed protection; (3) ground-based kinetic/non-kinetic systems; (4) counter-UAS; (5) counter-fixed/rotary wing aircraft; (6) counter-cruise missile; (7) interoperability with joint C2 networks; (8) 360-degree active/passive sensors; (9) systems/software enabling reduced staffing.
- (c) Fielding Requirement: (1) By September 30, 2027, field at least 4 sites, at least 2 in the U.S.; (2) in each of FY2028–FY2031, field at least 4 sites per year, at least 2 in the U.S. per year.
- (d) Report due to congressional defense committees by March 1, 2025.

**SEC. 153 – Plan for F-16 Simulators at Air National Guard Training Centers**
- (a) The Secretary of the Air Force, in coordination with the Director of the Air National Guard, shall develop a plan to fully fund establishment and maintenance of F-16 simulators at ANG training centers.
- (b) Plan elements: (1) cost estimate for maintaining existing simulators; (2) cost estimate for establishing simulators at centers required to have them but lacking them, including units converting from A-10 to F-16; (3) funding allocation plan, including proportion from Air Force vs. ANG.
- (c) Report due March 1, 2025, including the plan and an assessment from the Secretary and Chief of the National Guard Bureau evaluating readiness effects if simulators are not established/maintained.

**SEC. 154 – Plan for Sustainment and Recapitalization of Air National Guard Fighter Fleet**
- (a) The Secretary of the Air Force, in consultation with the Director of the ANG, shall develop a sustainment and recapitalization plan.
- (b) Plan elements: (1) identify each of the 25 ANG fighter squadrons existing on enactment date; (2) provide recapitalization plan for all squadrons at a similar rate as active component squadrons, with the same mix of legacy and advanced capability fighter aircraft; (3) establish a timetable disaggregated by squadron and fiscal year, identifying required funding; (4) assess budgetary effects on active components if implemented; (5) assess effects on operational and personnel readiness of active and reserve components, including ability to meet combatant commander requirements.
- (c) Report due July 1, 2025; unclassified with possible classified annex.
- (d) Definitions: “Advanced capability fighter aircraft” means next-generation air dominance or sixth-generation airframe (excluding unmanned); “fifth generation” means F-22 or F-35; “fighter aircraft” per § 9062(i)(2); “legacy capability fighter aircraft” means pre-fifth generation (F-16, F-15C/D, F-15E/EX, A-10).

**SEC. 161 – Modification to Air Force and Navy Use of Commercial Dual-Use Parts**
- Amends § 161 of the FY2023 NDAA (P.L. 117-263; 10 U.S.C. § 3453 note): (1) section heading modified; (2) inserts “new,” before “used” in subsection (a)(1); (3) inserts “, or from a certified production approval holder pursuant to part 21 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations” before the period in subsection (b)(2).

**SEC. 162 – Measures to Increase Supply Chain Resiliency for Small Unmanned Aerial Systems (sUAS)**
- (a) Within 180 days of enactment, the Secretary of Defense shall establish integrated measures to: (1) identify sUAS supply chain risks; (2) increase resiliency using domestic and allied/partner sources.
- (b) Elements: (1) Within 90 days and at least every 3 years thereafter until 2034, fully disassemble a Da Jiang Innovations or similar commercially available sUAS manufactured in a covered foreign country to: (A) create a component taxonomy by function, risk level, etc.; (B) help assess component risk. (2) Within 150 days, using the taxonomy, develop a supply chain risk framework to: (A) assess risk of each component to DoD networks/operations; (B) identify manufacturers in covered foreign countries and evaluate mitigation feasibility; (C) determine if any foreign companies should be included on the § 1260H list. (3) Within 180 days, develop a strategy for a secure/resilient domestic and allied supply chain including: (A) identification of non-covered-foreign-country sources and their capacity; (B) assessment of total DoD sUAS requirement; (C) plan to increase alternative source manufacturing capacity with estimated funding; (D) description of how existing DoD initiatives/programs can create alternative sources, including recommendations for using Defense Production Act authorities, IBAS program, loan guarantees, and incentivizing private investment.
- (c) Report due within 270 days, including: (1) list of components with security vulnerabilities; (2) description of risk framework; (3) recommendations for § 1260H list inclusion; (4) the full strategy. Unclassified with possible classified annex.
- (e) “Covered foreign country” defined per § 848(e) of FY2020 NDAA (P.L. 116-92; 10 U.S.C. § 4871 note).

**SEC. 163 – Policy on Qualifications of Contractors for Into-Plane Fuel Deliveries for Heavy-Lift Aircraft**
- (a) Within one year of enactment, the Director of the Defense Logistics Agency shall develop and implement a policy for acquisition planning for contracts providing into-plane procurement of an estimated 5,000,000 gallons or more of aviation fuel per year within the continental U.S. for heavy-lift aircraft.
- (b) The Director shall determine whether to use evaluation factors to assess fixed-based operator qualifications, which may include: (1) sufficient onsite fuel storage; (2) sufficient employees to service military customers; (3) capability for cargo on-load/off-load/handling (including dangerous goods) for all military aircraft sizes; (4) acceptable past performance; (5) other factors.
- (c) The Director shall consult with military departments in developing mission requirements at commercial airports.
- (d) “Heavy-lift aircraft” means maximum gross takeoff weight in excess of 107,000 pounds.

**SEC. 164 – Prohibition on Operation, Procurement, and Contracting Related to Foreign-Made LiDAR Technology**
- (a) Prohibition: The Secretary of Defense shall not operate or enter into/renew a contract for procurement of: (1) covered LiDAR technology that is (A) manufactured in a covered foreign country or by an entity domiciled there; (B) uses operating software developed in a covered foreign country or by an entity domiciled there; or (C) uses network connectivity/data storage located in or administered by an entity domiciled in a covered foreign country; or (2) a system incorporating/interfacing with/using such LiDAR technology.
- (b) Exemption: The prohibition does not apply to operations/procurement/contracting for intelligence, electronic warfare, and information warfare operations, testing, analysis, and training.
- (c) Waiver: The Secretary may waive on a case-by-case basis by certifying in writing to the congressional defense committees that the action is required in the national interest.
- (d) Effective Date: June 30, 2026.
- (e) Definitions: “Covered foreign country” means China, Iran, North Korea, Russia. “Covered LiDAR company” means Hesai Technology (or affiliates), entities on the Consolidated Screening List or § 1260h civil-military fusion list, or entities domiciled in a covered foreign country or subject to unmitigated foreign ownership/control/influence by a covered foreign country. “Covered LiDAR technology” means LiDAR technology and related services/equipment manufactured by a covered LiDAR company. “LiDAR” means a sensor that emits light to detect and measure range of surroundings.

**SEC. 165 – Limitation on Procurement of F-35 Aircraft Pending Certification**
- (a) Limitation: The Secretary of Defense may not accept or take delivery of covered F-35 aircraft in excess of the maximum quantities in subsection (c) until certifying compliance with 9 requirements, each requiring submission to Congress and implementation of a plan with actions/milestones for: (1) F-35 digital-twin models across the enterprise; (2) procurement of at least one new cooperative avionics flying test bed; (3) procurement/construction of a new F-35 mission software integration lab for concurrent TR-2/TR-3 testing; (4) resolution of all deficiencies/recommendations in the 2024 F-35 IOT&E report; (5) resolution of programmatic deficiencies associated with new F-35 mission system radar hardware/software; (6) resolution of deficiencies/recommendations in the F-35 software Independent Review Team report; (7) a corrective action plan addressing sustainment challenges and improving fleetwide mission capable/full mission capable rates, including (A) depot set-up and production capacity, (B) corrosion mitigation (parts, equipment, technical data, staffing), (C) improved asset/parts visibility and availability, (D) mechanisms to surge supply support and ensure logistics continuity in contested environments; (8) submission of all plans to committees; (9) meeting requirements of § 226(b)(5) and (c) of the FY2024 NDAA.
- (b) Plans submitted to Congress must include: (A) estimated total funds required; (B) realistic, event-driven schedules; (C) schedule risk assessment at minimum 80% confidence level. Unclassified with possible classified annex.
- (c) Maximum quantities: 30 F-35A, 9 F-35B, 9 F-35C.
- (d) Annual reports due April 1, 2025, and annually for five years thereafter, providing comprehensive updates on implementation of the plans.
- (e) “Covered F-35 aircraft” means new production F-35s authorized for procurement with FY2025 funds and fully funded by the U.S.

**SEC. 166 – Assessments of Inventory Requirements for Air-to-Air Missiles**
- (a) The Secretary of the Air Force and Secretary of the Navy, in coordination with combatant commanders, shall jointly assess sufficiency of established air-to-air missile inventory requirements.
- (b) Elements: (1) assess planned deliveries through 2029 and total available missiles by type each year; (2) assess combined requirements for CENTCOM, INDOPACOM, NORTHCOM, EUCOM at low/medium/high risk; (3) consider emerging surface-to-air defense and collaborative combat aircraft requirements; (4) consider sufficiency of planned acquisition through 2029; (5) consider whether continuing AMRAAM production through 2029 would enhance inventories; (6) develop recommendations to adjust planned missile mix, including assessment of extending range/capability of existing missiles.
- (c) Joint report due not later than April 1, 2025, summarizing results for each element. Unclassified with possible classified annex.

**SEC. 167 – Plan for Signals Intelligence Capabilities of Armed Overwatch Aircraft**
- (a) Within 180 days of enactment, the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Special Operations and Low Intensity Conflict and the Commander of USSOCOM shall jointly submit a plan for integrating signals intelligence capabilities on fielded armed overwatch aircraft.
- (b) Plan must: (1) define SIGINT requirements, including required capabilities and number of aircraft to be equipped; (2) articulate necessary resources by fiscal year; (3) include any other relevant matters.

**SEC. 201 – Authorization of Appropriations**
- Funds are authorized to be appropriated for FY2025 for DoD RDT&E as specified in the funding table in section 4201.

**SEC. 211 – Modification of Joint Energetics Transition Office Requirements**
- Amends 10 U.S.C. § 148(d) to read: (1) The Secretary shall ensure the Office is budgeted and funded sufficiently for staff and resources to carry out its responsibilities. (2) In budget justification materials for FY2027 and each fiscal year thereafter, the Secretary shall include a dedicated budget line item for implementation of subsection (a) and for testing/evaluation of energetic materials and technologies by the Office.

**SEC. 212 – Modification to Annual Report on Unfunded Priorities of USD(R&E)**
- Amends the second 10 U.S.C. § 222e: (1) in subsection (a), requires the Secretary of Defense to coordinate with the Secretaries of the military departments before submitting; (2) in subsection (e), adds a new paragraph (3) requiring that, for a military construction project, the project has reached 35 percent design.

**SEC. 213 – Modification to Defense Laboratory Education Partnerships**
- Amends 10 U.S.C. § 2194(b) by adding new paragraph (8): authority to enter into new and separate contracts, cooperative agreements, or grants with the institution to provide financial assistance for activities conducted under the partnership agreement.

**SEC. 214 – Extension of Global Research Watch Program**
- Amends 10 U.S.C. § 4066(f) by striking “September 30, 2025” and inserting “September 30, 2035”.

**SEC. 215 – Expansion of Authority for Technology Protection Features Activities**
- (a) Amends 10 U.S.C. § 4067(a) by striking “during the research and development phase of such system” and inserting “to increase ally and partner military capability or improve coalition interoperability”.
- (b) Amends subsection (b): (1) redesignates (2) as (3); (2) inserts new (2) requiring any contract for design/development of an exportability feature to include a cost-sharing provision requiring the contractor to bear half the cost (or other portion as the Secretary considers appropriate upon showing of good cause); (3) modifies new (3) to apply to both designated systems and exportability features.

**SEC. 216 – Modification to Personnel Management Authority to Attract Experts**
- Amends 10 U.S.C. § 4092: (1) section heading changed to “science, engineering, and certain other disciplines”; (2) adds new subsection (a)(11) authorizing the Director of the Office of Strategic Capital to carry out a personnel management program to recruit eminent experts in finance and investment; (3) in subsection (b), increases position limits: (D) Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering from 5 to 20 (max 5 admin/management); (E) Defense Innovation Unit from 5 to 35 (max 5 admin/management); (H) from 15 to 25; adds new (K) for Office of Strategic Capital up to 30 positions; amends (2)(A) to allow pay up to 150% of Vice President’s total annual compensation for appointees under (B), (D), (E), (H), and (K).

**SEC. 217 – Codification of the Laboratory Quality Enhancement Program**
- (a) Adds new 10 U.S.C. § 4128.
- (a) Program: The Secretary, acting through USD(R&E), shall carry out the “Laboratory Quality Enhancement Program” to establish panels to: (A) review and make recommendations on policies/practices, new initiatives, and new interpretations of law to enhance STRL directors’ management; (B) support implementation of initiatives; (C) conduct assessments/data analysis on effectiveness of authorities.
- (b) Panels: (1) Personnel, workforce development, and talent management; (2) Facilities, equipment, and infrastructure; (3) Research strategy, technology transfer, and industry/university partnerships; (4) Governance and oversight processes.
- (c) Composition: Panels 1–3 composed of subject matter experts from service labs/research centers, Defense Agencies, OUSD(R&E), and other entities. Panel 4 composed of at least one member from each STRL and other members.
- (d) Governance: Chairperson selected by panel members. Panels transmit information/findings to the Science and Technology Executive Committee.
- (e) Interpretation of Law: USD(R&E) shall issue regulations on meaning/scope/implementation/applicability of statutes relating to STRLs, emphasizing maximum operational flexibility for directors, consulting with service secretaries, and seeking recommendations from Panel 4.
- (f) “Science and technology reinvention laboratory” defined per § 4121.
- (b) Repeals § 211 of the FY2017 NDAA (P.L. 114-328; 10 U.S.C. note prec. 4121).

**SEC. 218 – Modification to Consortium on Additive Manufacturing**
- Amends § 223(c) of the FY2024 NDAA (P.L. 118-31; 10 U.S.C. § 4841 note) by adding new paragraph (7): develop a process to certify new materials and processes for fabricating flight critical parts and initiate planning for a rapidly deployable additive manufacturing system capable of fabricating replacement safety-critical parts for military aircraft/UAVs in severely restricted access environments.

**SEC. 219 – Modification to Continuous Capability Development and Delivery Program for F-35**
- Amends § 225(b) of the FY2024 NDAA (P.L. 118-31): (1) changes designated aircraft from “two F-35A, two F-35B, and two F-35C” to “a total of not fewer than nine F-35A, F-35B, or F-35C aircraft”; (2) changes “Lot 19” to “Lot 18”.

**SEC. 220 – Modifications to Test Program for DDG(X) Destroyer Engineering Plant**
- Amends § 221 of the FY2022 NDAA (P.L. 117-81): (1) adds requirement that a minimum of two motor technologies with comparable efficiency/weight/space characteristics providing a minimum of 40 megawatts of reserve power (in excess of propulsion and ship service at patrol speed) shall be tested in full scale to mitigate risk and provide competition prior to down select; (2) strikes paragraph (1) and inserts new (1) specifying “Two electrical propulsion motor technologies”; (3) inserts “that incorporates two propulsion motor technology options” before the period in (d)(1).

**SEC. 221 – Improvements Relating to Defining, Identifying, and Planning the AI Workforce**
- (a) Amends § 230 of the FY2020 NDAA (P.L. 116-92; 10 U.S.C. note prec. 501) by striking subsection (c) and inserting new (c): (1) Not later than April 30, 2025, the Secretary shall appoint a civilian official known as the “Chief Digital Engineering Recruitment and Management Officer of the Department of Defense” responsible for developing/implementing the policy and implementation plan. (2) Additional responsibilities: (A) fully define and identify the DoD AI workforce by (i) clarifying roles and relationship to innovation/digital workforce, (ii) coding AI roles in workforce data systems, (iii) developing a qualification program; (B) update the DoD Human Capital Operating Plan consistent with the Strategic Management Plan and Annual Performance Plan relating to AI workforce issues. (3) Appointment expires September 30, 2030.
- (b) Within 90 days of enactment, the Secretary shall submit a report updating activities under the § 230(b) implementation plan.
- (c) Within 240 days of enactment, the Secretary shall brief the committees on: (1) positions included in the AI workforce; (2) positions not identified that should be included; (3) positions requiring AI-skilled personnel; (4) current state of the AI workforce; (5) planned/proposed future requirements.

**SEC. 222 – Modification to Artificial Intelligence Education Strategy**
- Amends § 256 of the FY2020 NDAA (P.L. 116-92) by adding new subsection (d): (1) Within 180 days of enactment of the FY2025 NDAA, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, in coordination with USD(P&R), shall: (A) develop distance education courses on (i) foundational AI/ML concepts, and (ii) responsible and ethical design, development, acquisition, deployment, and use of AI/ML applications; (B) make courses available to members of the Armed Forces. (2) Within 270 days of enactment, the Secretary shall submit a progress report to the committees.

**SEC. 223 – Modification of CVN-73 to Support Fielding of MQ-25**
- Amends § 219 of the FY2019 NDAA (P.L. 115-232) to require modification of the compartments and infrastructure of the aircraft carrier designated CVN-73 to support fielding of the MQ-25 unmanned aerial vehicle before its planned deployment date.

**SEC. 224 – Modification to Innovators Information Repository**
- Amends § 220 of the FY2019 NDAA (P.L. 115-232; 10 U.S.C. § 4061 note prec.): (1) inserts “Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, the Defense Innovation Unit, and the” before “Defense Technical Information Center” in subsection (a); (2) inserts “in accordance with subsection (e)” in subsection (b); (3) amends subsection (c)(1) to require coordination across DoD to focus on small business concerns including SBIR/STTR participants, participants in the § 834 pilot or Rapid Defense Experimentation Reserve, and nontraditional defense contractors working with research/innovation/advanced project entities; adds subparagraphs (E) date of initial award and (F) dates of any additional awards; (4) adds new subsection (e) requiring updates not less frequently than once each fiscal quarter, subject to appropriations.

**SEC. 225 – Duties of CDAO Governing Council Relating to AI Models and Advanced AI Technologies**
- Amends § 238(d)(3)(E) of the FY2019 NDAA (P.L. 115-232; 10 U.S.C. note prec. 4061) by inserting new clause (x): With respect to AI models and advanced AI technologies: (I) identify and assess models/technologies that could pose a national security risk if accessed by an adversary; (II) develop strategies to prevent unauthorized access/usage by adversary countries; (III) make recommendations to Congress and relevant Federal agencies for legislative or administrative action.

**SEC. 226 – Ensuring Compliance with DoD Policy When Awarding Research Grants**
- Amends § 1286 of the FY2019 NDAA (P.L. 115-232; 10 U.S.C. § 4001 note): (1) technical correction in (d)(1)(B); (2) redesignates (e)–(h) as (f)–(i); (3) inserts new (e) requiring annual reviews: not later than March 30, 2025, and annually thereafter, each head of a DoD component awarding research grants shall review a representative sample of prior-year grants for policy compliance, and USD(R&E) shall carry out a separate review of a representative sample; (4) modifies redesignated (f) to add reporting on the periodic reviews, including total number of grants awarded, number of reviews, description of processes, and assessment of issues/ list of non-compliant grants.

**SEC. 227 – Extension and Modification of Directed Energy Working Group**
- Amends § 219(d) of the FY2017 NDAA (P.L. 114-328; 10 U.S.C. § 4205 note): (1) adds to paragraph (6) briefing requirements: cost data and associated program elements for each organization across the FYDP, and information on enabling work (vehicle/software integration, C2/targeting architectures, infrastructure, workforce training); (2) in paragraph (7), strikes “4 years” and inserts “9 years”.

**SEC. 228 – National Defense Economic Competition Research Council**
- (a) Within 90 days of enactment, the Secretary of Defense shall establish a council to identify, evaluate, and coordinate existing research or propose new topics relating to economic competition activities (economic coercion, manipulation, etc.) that undermine the national defense strategy.
- (b) Within 120 days, the Secretary shall issue a charter with a mission including: (1) analyzing ongoing/proposed government and academic research; (2) proposing new research areas; (3) informing DoD tools to defend against economic competition; (4) assessing data needs/shortfalls; (5) convening groups (academia, nonprofits, commercial, government, international partners); (6) other activities as deemed appropriate.
- (c) Co-chairs: USD(Policy), USD(R&E), USD(A&S). Participants include specified offices (e.g., Air Force Office of Commercial and Economic Assessment, Office of Strategic Capital, DIU, DARPA, Minerva Research Initiative, etc.).
- (d) Council shall regularly solicit input from Joint Staff and combatant commands.
- (e) Terminates December 31, 2035.

### SEC. 5603. GOVERNMENT-WIDE STUDY.
- **Purpose & Mechanism:** Directs the Administrator (of General Services, implied by context) to coordinate a government-wide study on creating a security assessment process for "high-security leased adjacent space" before entering into a lease or novation with a "covered entity" for a Federal tenant.
- **Key Definitions:** "Agency" is defined by 5 U.S.C. 551.
- **Study Contents:**
    - **Mandatory:** Evaluate a threat-level assessment process for each occupancy, including site visits, interviews, and other activities determined by the Federal Protective Service Director.
    - **Permissive:** May include a process to collect information on immediate, highest-level, or beneficial owners of a covered entity, including name, address, and an identity-verifying number/document.
- **Working Group:**
    - **Deadline:** Must be established within 90 days of enactment.
    - **Composition:** Administrator coordinates with the Federal Protective Service Director, DHS Secretary, OMB Director, and other relevant entities.
    - **Compensation:** Members serve without compensation.
    - **Sunset:** Terminates upon submission of the report under subsection (f).
- **Protections & Limitations:**
    - Information collected is not to be made public.
    - No entity in the U.S. is required to provide information.
    - No Federal entity is authorized to mandate information gathering unless specifically authorized by law.
    - Information from the security assessment process (subsection (b)(1)) cannot be used for law enforcement purposes.
- **Reporting:** A report is due to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee and the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee within 2 years of enactment, describing the study's results and how applicable privacy laws and First/Fourth Amendment rights would be upheld.
- **Funding:** No additional funds are authorized.

### SEC. 5611. DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY NORTHERN BORDER MISSION CENTER.
- **Purpose & Mechanism:** Establishes a DHS Northern Border Mission Center as a forward-deployed operations support center for domain awareness, information sharing, intelligence, training, and stakeholder engagement.
- **Deadline:** The Secretary of Homeland Security shall establish the Center within 1 year of enactment.
- **Location:** Must be along the northern border, collocated with an existing U.S. Border Patrol sector headquarters, an Air and Marine Operations branch, a U.S. Coast Guard air station, and other DHS activities.
- **Components:** Collocates personnel from CBP, USCG, ICE Homeland Security Investigations, and other DHS components as determined by the Secretary. Additional federal, state, tribal, local, and international partners may be collocated.
- **Functions:** Includes serving as a coordination mechanism for the Northern Border Strategy; a training location; a testing ground for border security technology; establishing quick reaction air and marine capabilities; supporting counter-UAS operations (consistent with 6 U.S.C. 124n, with no new authority granted); ensuring privacy and civil rights compliance; and identifying challenges on the noncontiguous border with Canada and maritime border with Russia.
- **Reporting:**
    - **Annual Report:** Due 180 days after establishment and annually thereafter to specified committees, describing activities, personnel levels, needed resources, and needed assets/authorities.
    - **Quarterly Report:** On temporary duty assignments of U.S. Border Patrol agents, including numbers, duration, and originating/assigned sectors.
    - **Large UAS Report:** Due within 1 year of enactment on the Department's operation of large UAS, including recommendations for enabling operations based at the Center.
- **Rules of Construction:** The Center is separate from the Secretary's authority under 6 U.S.C. 348. Nothing affects the Commandant of the Coast Guard's authority under titles 14 or 46 U.S.C.
- **Sunset:** The section ceases to be effective on October 1, 2027.
- **Funding:** No additional funds are authorized.
